Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract in `README.md`, then use the wake-visual-signals skill because this task explicitly requires inspecting rollout evidence before changing the target policy. I’ll stay within this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring configurations.

The visual-signal skill requires anchoring images to the written score and diagnostics first. I’m now inventorying only the provided guidance, sampled solver evidence, inherited logs, and current candidate so the diagnosis and eventual edit are traceable to allowed sources.

The supplied metrics show a finite but clearly non-navigating seed: it briefly approached to `8.61L`, then moved `13.30L` downward and exited after only `50.13` released time, with both acceleration channels hitting the hard limit. Per the skill, I’m checking the shared initial wake and then the released sequence before deciding whether the failure is advection, propulsion, steering, or saturation dominated.

The keyframes resolve the main failure: the fish begins above/right of the target, initially points diagonally toward the wake, then turns nearly vertical and self-propels rapidly through the bottom boundary without entering the useful second-row region. The wake is developed at release, but the `-13.30L` vertical versus `-3.55L` horizontal displacement and repeated high-curvature body shapes indicate target-blind thrust plus saturated oscillation, not passive advection, is driving the exit. I’m checking the exposed state schema now so the replacement uses legitimate normalized body-frame target feedback.

The flow cross-check changes the diagnosis slightly: mean world-frame local flow `(-0.041, -0.241)` nearly matches mean fish velocity `(-0.073, -0.263)`, leaving only `(0.031, 0.022)` mean relative flow. So the saturated gait expends heavily without establishing useful target-relative motion while the fish is entrained downward. I’ll record that evidence and a falsifiable bearing-steering hypothesis before touching the policy, as the skill requires.

The provenance note and durable guidance lesson are now in place. I’m replacing the seed with one candidate only: the same clock-free oscillator family, but with bounded body-frame bearing steering through mean tail curvature and an internal command ceiling below the episode’s safety cap.

The candidate is non-empty and all eight referenced `params` fields are declared by `target_policy_params()`. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now—semantic guidance check, lightweight Julia contract evaluation, then the workspace boundary guard. These checks do not run CFD.

The first mandated check exposed a workspace-rendering defect rather than a content defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, while the checker requires exactly one copied-parent marker. I’m inspecting the checker’s matching rule and will make the smallest in-workspace repair needed for an unambiguous parent, then rerun it.

The semantic guidance check passes. The Julia contract check is currently blocked by the environment (`julia: command not found`, plus unrelated login-shell SSH setup noise), not by the policy. I’m locating an installed Julia binary without running any simulation; if none exists, I’ll still complete the deterministic schema/static checks and report the infrastructure limitation precisely.

The boundary guard passes, confirming the solver tree differs from its baseline only at the permitted candidate file. No Julia executable is present in the standard paths or local Julia locations, so I’m finishing with the checker’s deterministic source-level parameter-schema guard plus bounded-output probes at aligned and extreme bearings; this is verification only, not CFD.

Implemented exactly one multi-wake policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded body-frame bearing steering, moderated oscillator, and sub-envelope acceleration cap.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, evidence boundary, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:38): reusable negative lesson from the saturated, downward-entrained seed.

Guidance, schema, finite-output, and boundary checks pass. The Julia runtime check could not execute because `julia` is not installed; no CFD was run. I also removed the duplicated assigned-parent marker in `README.md` so the mandated guidance checker could resolve the parent unambiguously.
